excerpts.text: - [x] Math: required checked owner holds 39 singleton, numeric adapter and exact-summation declarations; 19 scoped emission boundaries and canonical enumeration/lookup replace flat metadata. Merged in #1681 after all required main/desktop gates and exact-head review passed. Original broad verification passed 798 distinct cases including 82 new cases; fresh verification after Number merged passed 248 focused cases and regenerated 26 IL-verified saved comparisons preserving 27,856 method bodies/exception regions, with 24 exact standalone executions and two hosted outputs. Build, source ownership audit and quality gates passed. The full 17-file implementation review found only a stale comment, corrected and incrementally reviewed. A later Windows CI failure exposed an unchanged lifecycle fixture that assumed rejection reporting preceded fixed timers. Both delayed-rejection controls reproduced its exact failure; the test now schedules catch attachment from the actual event and reports completion at beforeExit. All 65 related tests pass locally with the strict output assertion and timeout unchanged. That one-file correction received exact-head review with no actionable findings; earlier implementation evidence retains its original provenance. Final CI passed 21,533 core tests plus one Windows-only skip on Linux and 21,531 core tests plus three existing platform skips on Windows, with 129 GUI passes per platform and zero failures. All 82 Math cases, four lifecycle variants, both generator modes and both fork IPC modes passed on both platforms. Product source and CI budgets were unchanged by the fixture correction. Singleton/adapter/Random/exact-sum ordering, descriptors, numeric algorithms and coercion order are preserved; construction helpers and BCL metadata stay local. The early descriptor fallback keeps its historically absent sumPrecise target. Existing global Math identity, aliased nonfinite summation and adapter signed-zero behavior remain baseline compatibility limitations, not conformance fixes. All broader ownership migrations and final audits remain required.
